sentences.en: Hello, and as L.P.
sentences.zh: 你好，正如L·P·

sentences.en: Hartley famously said, the past is a foreign country.
sentences.zh: 哈特利那句名言所说，过去是一个异国他乡。

sentences.en: They do things differently there.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里行事方式与我们不同。

sentences.en: But do they?
sentences.zh: 但真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Today on our episode of The Rest is History, we want to look at the very recent past prompted by the return to Netflix of The Crown.
sentences.zh: 今天在我们的节目《历史其余部分》中，我们想探讨一下最近刚过去的时代，这灵感来自于Netflix剧集《王冠》的回归。

sentences.en: But before we come to that, and I know, Dominic, you'll be straining at least about this because recent British history is very much your subject, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但在我们进入正题之前——我知道，多米尼克，你肯定对此跃跃欲试，因为英国近代史正是你的专长，不是吗？

sentences.en: So you're going to have lots to say.
sentences.zh: 所以你一定有很多话要说。

sentences.en: I just wanted to say to thank everybody who's listening for having helped us get off to such a great start.
sentences.zh: 我只是想对所有收听节目的听众表示感谢，感谢你们帮助我们有了一个如此棒的开端。

sentences.en: It's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: We were a bit nervous about launching this, but we're thrilled that so many of you are out there, are listening and emailing in and tweeting and contributing.
sentences.zh: 我们对推出这个节目其实还有点紧张，但看到有这么多人在关注、收听、发邮件、发推特并参与进来，我们感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And please do keep that going.
sentences.zh: 请大家务必继续保持这份热情。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's quite a surprise, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 是的，这真是个惊喜，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: I was expecting a torrent of abuse.
sentences.zh: 我本来以为会招来铺天盖地的谩骂。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I obviously get torrents of abuse naturally on a sort of daily basis anyway.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我日常生活中本来就自然而然地会受到各种谩骂。

sentences.en: So this is a nice break for me.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说这算是个不错的调剂。

sentences.en: Well, I was kind of expecting tumbleweed, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我其实有点期待看到冷清得像滚草掠过一样的场面。

sentences.en: So neither abuse nor tumbleweed.
sentences.zh: 结果既没有谩骂，也没有冷场。

sentences.en: So do please keep letting us know what you think.
sentences.zh: 所以请大家继续让我们听到你们的想法。

sentences.en: Should we read out some tweets?
sentences.zh: 我们要不要读几条推特？

sentences.en: That would be a very good idea.
sentences.zh: 那是个非常好的主意。

sentences.en: Should we engage with the great British public?
sentences.zh: 我们要不要与伟大的英国公众互动一下？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So we have somebody, Alex Burson, he wrote, thanks for doing it.
sentences.zh: 有一位叫亚历克斯·伯森的听众写道，谢谢你们制作这个节目。

sentences.en: The rest of this history is great.
sentences.zh: 《历史其余部分》太棒了。

sentences.en: For your amusement, Stephen the Great of Moldova was sanctified by the Orthodox Church in the 1990s and is now Stephen the Great and Saint.
sentences.zh: 为了博君一笑，摩尔多瓦的伟大斯蒂芬在20世纪90年代被东正教封圣，现在被称为“伟大斯蒂芬圣人”。

sentences.en: He had four wives, as Saint should, and was known to be quick to spill blood.
sentences.zh: 他有四个妻子，不愧为圣人，而且以行事杀伐果断闻名。

sentences.en: But he built churches and defended Christianity.
sentences.zh: 但他建造了教堂，捍卫了基督教。

sentences.en: He was quite great.
sentences.zh: 他确实很伟大。

sentences.en: It's just that the Saint is both a late edition and amusing in the context of episode one.
sentences.zh: 只不过“圣人”这个头衔是后来加上去的，在第一集的语境下显得很有趣。

sentences.en: So there you go.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, being a Saint and great, I mean, that's square in the circle, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，既当圣人又当伟人，这简直是在方中求圆，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, he did a bit of everything, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他什么都涉猎了一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Polymath.
sentences.zh: 博学者。

sentences.en: We also have a message from Andrew Walker.
sentences.zh: 我们还收到了安德鲁·沃克的一条留言。

sentences.en: He's been wondering about academic reassessment of Nero.
sentences.zh: 他一直在思考学术界对尼禄的重新评价。

sentences.en: Oh, good.
sentences.zh: 哦，太好了。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 好极了。

sentences.en: Academic reassessment of Nero.
sentences.zh: 学术界对尼禄的重新评价。

sentences.en: That's very much my thing.
sentences.zh: 这正合我意。

sentences.en: This person exists.
sentences.zh: 这个人是真实存在的。

sentences.en: He's not you under a false name, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他可不是你用假名注册的号。

sentences.en: That's my sock puppet.
sentences.zh: 那是我的小号。

sentences.en: He's heard about it on another podcast, Boo His.
sentences.zh: 他在另一个播客里听到了这个说法，嘘，真差劲。

sentences.en: It amounts to, well, he was rather popular with the plebs.
sentences.zh: 归纳起来就是，嗯，他在平民中相当受欢迎。

sentences.en: People after him invoked him to boost their appeal and his critics were fake news from the swamp.
sentences.zh: 他身后的人利用他来提升自己的吸引力，而批评他的人则是来自沼泽的假新闻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, basically.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Can't disagree with that.
sentences.zh: 对此我无可反驳。

sentences.en: And then we've got a lovely, lovely comment from Emma Salisbury.
sentences.zh: 然后我们收到了埃玛·索尔兹伯里一条非常可爱、非常温暖的评论。

sentences.en: I'm listening to this right now.
sentences.zh: 我正在收听这个节目。

sentences.en: It's rather nostalgically like being at a friendly dinner party with fellow historians, even though Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook can't hear me chiming in.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉非常怀旧，就像和志同道合的历史学家朋友们坐在一起开一个友好的晚宴，尽管汤姆·霍兰德和多米尼克·桑布鲁克听不到我的插话。

sentences.en: So that speaks to somebody who's clearly never been at a dinner party with historians.
sentences.zh: 这说明她显然从来没有和历史学家一起吃过晚宴。

sentences.en: The mood of bitterness and rancor.
sentences.zh: 那种充满痛苦和怨恨的气氛。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, bitterness and rancor is what we're all about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，痛苦和怨恨正是我们的特色。

sentences.en: So anyway, you can, this dinner party, this friendly dinner party, do join in.
sentences.zh: 总之，你完全可以加入这场晚宴，这场友好的晚宴。

sentences.en: You can chime in, tweet us, hashtag TheRestIsHistory.
sentences.zh: 你可以插话，给我们发推特，带话题#TheRestIsHistory。

sentences.en: And also, very excitingly, we've got an email address now, RestIsHistoryPod at gmail.com.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一个非常令人兴奋的消息，我们现在有一个邮箱地址了，RestIsHistoryPod@gmail.com。

sentences.en: RestIsHistoryPod at gmail.com.
sentences.zh: RestIsHistoryPod at gmail.com.

sentences.en: And I like that idea of the ultimate historical dinner party.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢终极历史晚宴这个主意的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that would be a good idea for a future episode.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这可以作为未来某一期节目的好点子。

sentences.en: Say, what, kind of, people from across the range of history, who would make the ideal dinner party?
sentences.zh: 比方说，邀请历史上各个时期的人，谁才是理想的晚宴宾客？

sentences.en: Genghis Khan.
sentences.zh: 成吉思汗。

sentences.en: No, he'd be terrible.
sentences.zh: 不，他可太可怕了。

sentences.en: He'd chop your head off and drink out of your skull.
sentences.zh: 他会砍下你的头，然后用你的头骨喝酒。

sentences.en: That's a terrible idea.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: Anyway, listen, we won't, we're not going to get on to that.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，听着，我们不会，我们不打算讨论这个。

sentences.en: Let's get on to The Crown.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈《王冠》吧。

sentences.en: Yes, let's.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们谈谈这个。

sentences.en: Because I'm guessing you have, do you have views on this?
sentences.zh: 因为我猜你对这事有看法，你看过《王冠》吗？

sentences.en: Have you seen The Crown?
sentences.zh: 你看过《王冠》吗？

sentences.en: As you well know, Tom, I have never seen The Crown.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，正如你很清楚的那样，我从来没看过《王冠》。

sentences.en: I have not seen so much as a minute of The Crown.
sentences.zh: 我连一分钟的《王冠》都没看过。

sentences.en: Why would I?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要看？

sentences.en: I mean, I spend, you know, my working day thinking about Harold Wilson or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我的工作时间都在思考哈罗德·威尔逊之类的事情。

sentences.en: And Dominic, has the fact that you have never seen The Crown, has it prevented you from writing about it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你从来没看过《王冠》这件事，有没有妨碍你对它进行写作？

sentences.en: No, obviously not.
sentences.zh: 没有，显然没有。

sentences.en: I mean, that would be, that would be anathema to all I stand for.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那将与我所坚信的一切背道而驰。

sentences.en: Have you, have you, have you just written an enormous spread about the 80s to coincide with the new series of The Crown set in the 80s?
sentences.zh: 你是不是刚刚写了一篇长篇大论来介绍80年代，好配合以80年代为背景的新一季《王冠》的上映？

sentences.en: No, I haven't.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有。

sentences.en: But I have given, I have given a long interview to BBC History Magazine.
sentences.zh: 但我接受了英国广播公司历史杂志的长篇采访。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 原来如此。

sentences.en: But they know I haven't seen it.
sentences.zh: 但他们知道我没看过。

sentences.en: So they describe it to me over the phone.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在电话里把剧情描述给我听。

sentences.en: They tell me what happens and I tell them what I think of it.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我发生了什么，然后我告诉他们我对这些事的看法。

sentences.en: And I think it works very well.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这效果非常不错。

sentences.en: And just to make it clear to the listeners,
sentences.zh: 为了向听众澄清一下，

sentences.en: you've written a highly acclaimed series of books about modern British history that exactly cover the span of the decades that The Crown has covered.
sentences.zh: 你写过一套广受好评的英国现代史书籍，正好涵盖了《王冠》所涉及的几十年。

sentences.en: And your most recent book was, it was what, it was kind of like 7,000 page volume about three, the first three years of the Thatcher government.
sentences.zh: 你最近的一本书是关于什么题材的，大概是一本长达7000页的关于撒切尔政府最初三年的专著。

sentences.en: So from 79 to 82.
sentences.zh: 也就是从1979年到1982年。

sentences.en: So, so, so bang in the, bang in the middle of, of, of that is, is the summer of 1981, which of course has the Royal Wedding.
sentences.zh: 因此，正处于这一切正中央的，正是1981年的夏天，当然，那年举行了皇家婚礼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, the Royal Wedding is obviously a big deal for The Crown, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，皇家婚礼对《王冠》来说显然是一件大事，对吧？

sentences.en: Diana and all that.
sentences.zh: 戴安娜以及诸如此类的事。

sentences.en: Carry on.
sentences.zh: 接着说。

sentences.en: And it's a bigger deal for The Crown than it is for your book.
sentences.zh: 对《王冠》而言，它比对你的书更重要。

sentences.en: It would be fair to say.
sentences.zh: 这样说算是公正的。

sentences.en: Well, it is mentioned in my book.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的书里确实提到了这件事。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a, there is a whole section about the Royal Wedding, but I'm kind of more, I mean, to be honest with you, Tom, cakes, dresses, you know, page boys,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，里面有一个专门的章节讲述皇家婚礼，但老实说，汤姆，蛋糕、礼服、伴童这些东西，

sentences.en: that sort of stuff fills me with utter gloom and, and misery.
sentences.zh: 那种事情让我感到无比的沮丧和痛苦。

sentences.en: So when I talked about it in my book, it was more, what did people make of it?
sentences.zh: 所以在书里谈到它时，我更多是在探讨：人们是怎么看待它的？

sentences.en: What was the meaning of it?
sentences.zh: 它的意义何在？

sentences.en: And also actually putting it against the background of all this other stuff, which is so interesting, which is going on in 81.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上还要把它放在1981年发生的其他同样有趣的背景下去对比。

sentences.en: So the riots, the recession, the cricket, of course, which we'll come to later, this sort of tumultuous year, you know, 1981 is one of those years, I suppose,
sentences.zh: 比如骚乱、经济衰退，当然还有板球——我们稍后会谈到——这是一个波澜起伏的年份，你知道的，1981年就是那种年份，我想，

sentences.en: a little bit like sort of 1968 or something that has a, has a meaning beyond.
sentences.zh: 有点像1968年左右的年份，具有超越本身的意义。

sentences.en: Or 2020, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 或者也许就像2020年。

sentences.en: Or 2020, exactly.
sentences.zh: 或者说正是2020年。

sentences.en: I think it's a, you can make a reasonable case that 1981 was the grimmest year in our lifetimes.
sentences.zh: 我认为完全可以合情合理地认为1981年是我们一生中最严峻的一年。

sentences.en: And actually grimmer than 2020, because 2020 is worldwide, whereas 1981 was just, you know, it was Britain that was uniquely in a terrible mess.
sentences.zh: 事实上甚至比2020年更严峻，因为2020年是全球性的，而1981年仅仅是，你知道的，只有英国陷入了独一无二的惨淡境地。

sentences.en: So, I mean, the key thing about the Royal Wedding, everyone said it was like a fairy tale.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于皇家婚礼的关键点在于，所有人都说它就像童话一样。

sentences.en: And the irony about that is, is partly that the backdrop is this, you know, Britain in a state of complete turmoil, unemployment, rioting, and so on.
sentences.zh: 而其中的讽刺之处部分在于，它的背景是英国正处于一片彻底的混乱、失业、暴乱之中，等等。

sentences.en: But also the fact, of course, that, that the marriage was going to go terribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 但同样讽刺的是，这段婚姻注定会以悲剧收场。

sentences.en: And I just wondered, before we get, before we get onto the kind of historical context for 1981 provides,
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，在我们探讨1981年所提供的历史背景之前，

sentences.en: what's your view as a historian of modern Britain about the way in which the story of the Royal Family has kind of become like the matter of Britain that, you know,
sentences.zh: 作为一个英国现代史学家，你如何看待王室的故事变成了一种类似于“英国事务”的存在，你知道的，

sentences.en: like the matter of Britain in the Middle Ages was the story of King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 就像中世纪的“英国事务”是亚瑟王的故事一样。

sentences.en: That in a way, for lots of people, the story of King Arthur was, was more real, you know, they knew more about that than they knew anything about, you know,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，对许多人来说，亚瑟王的故事更加真实，你知道的，他们对那个故事的了解，要超过他们对中世纪英格兰实际发生的事情的了解。

sentences.en: what was actually happening in medieval England.
sentences.zh: 中世纪英格兰实际发生的事。

sentences.en: And there's, there's a kind of slight sense with, you know, that globally, what people know about British history is kind of, you know, and the story of Diana in particular,
sentences.zh: 在某种微妙的意义上，全球范围内人们对英国历史的了解，尤其是戴安娜的故事，

sentences.en: it's kind of like the modern matter of Britain.
sentences.zh: 它有点像是现代的“英国事务”。

sentences.en: People know about the story of Diana, it's become this mythic story.
sentences.zh: 人们了解戴安娜的故事，它已经变成了一个神话般的故事。

sentences.en: It's, does that have any historical significance?
sentences.zh: 这具有任何历史意义吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what does that say about Britain's role in the world?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这说明了英国在世界上的什么角色？

sentences.en: Okay, so I think that's true of Diana, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我认为这对戴安娜来说是成立的，对吧？

sentences.en: I think that's true that you can take the story of Diana and you can say, but you can also tease out sort of historical meanings about, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以把戴安娜的故事拿出来这么说，但你也可以从中梳理出一些历史意义，比如，

sentences.en: the sentimentalisation of British culture.
sentences.zh: 英国文化的感伤化。

sentences.en: Diana obviously played a big part in the sort of a new kind of, or a renewed kind of emotionalism in Britain's sort of public life.
sentences.zh: 戴安娜在英国公共生活中那种新的、或是重新焕发的情感主义中显然扮演了重要角色。

sentences.en: You know, sort of embracing aid sufferers and so on, you know, doing things that the, the, the monarchy or the, or the public figures wouldn't have done 10 or 20 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 比如说拥抱艾滋病患者等等，去做那些十年前或二十年前君主或公众人物绝不会去做的事情。

sentences.en: So she's sort of, she is an important figure in that context, obviously.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种背景下，她显然是一个重要人物。

sentences.en: But the royal family more generally, I'm not so sure.
sentences.zh: 但至于王室本身，我就没那么确定了。

sentences.en: So I agree with you, there are things that are, that people care more about than the usual sort of political events.
sentences.zh: 所以我同意你的看法，有些事情人们比常规的政治事件更加关心。

sentences.en: Sport is actually a really good example of that.
sentences.zh: 体育其实就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: So a lot of people, when they make sense of the recent past, they don't think about general elections and governments.
sentences.zh: 所以许多人在理解近代史时，想到的不是大选和政府。

sentences.en: They think about World Cups and, you know, how their team got on and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们想到的是世界杯，以及他们支持的球队表现如何之类的事情。

sentences.en: And music, again, you ask anybody about their, their youth or the, you know, if they grew up in the 60s or the 70s, it's often music that they turn to as their cultural references.
sentences.zh: 还有音乐，同样地，你问任何人关于他们的青春，或者如果他们是在60年代或70年代长大的人，他们往往会把音乐作为他们的文化参照。

sentences.en: And they'll say, well, the 60s ended when the Beatles broke up or, you know, the 70s ended when, you know, Sid Vicious died or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，60年代在披头士解散时结束了，或者说70年代在席德·维瑟斯去世时结束了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: People will look on those things as the sort of, the sort of chronological structuring, I guess, for the recent paSt.
sentences.zh: 人们会将这些事情视为近代史的某种时间结构，我想是的。

sentences.en: So I'm not so sure that the monarchy is the key one that I would go for.
sentences.zh: 所以我不太确定君主制是否是我会选择的关键点。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe it's because I don't really care that much about the sort of royal story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许是因为我其实并不是那么关心皇室的故事吧。

sentences.en: It's interesting you talk about music because actually the thing for me that's interesting about the 80s is that it's when I was a teenager.
sentences.zh: 你谈论音乐这很有趣，因为对我来说，关于80年代有趣的地方在于那是我的青少年时期。

sentences.en: So I was becoming kind of aware of politics.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始对政治有所意识。

sentences.en: I remember there was Not the Nine O'Clock News, which is kind of satire show, and they did Not the Royal Wedding.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时有一个叫《非九点钟新闻》的节目，那是个讽刺类节目，他们制作了《非皇家婚礼》。

sentences.en: And it was kind of like the first disrespectful treatment of the royal family that I'd come across.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是第一次让我接触到对王室的大不敬处理。

sentences.en: And I remember, you know, I was kind of 13, thought it was, thought it was great.
sentences.zh: 我记得，当时我大概13岁，觉得这节目太棒了。

sentences.en: But what I also remember is that there was a series on, I think on Radio 1 at the time, it's called 25 Years of Rock.
sentences.zh: 但我也记得，当时广播一台（Radio 1）上有一个系列节目，叫做《摇滚25年》。

sentences.en: And it ran from 1955 to 1979.
sentences.zh: 它的时间跨度从1955年一直到1979年。

sentences.en: And it, it kind of set current affairs to a soundtrack of the music of that particular year.
sentences.zh: 它把时事背景配上了特定年份的音乐原声带。

sentences.en: And it stopped in 79.
sentences.zh: 而它在79年就结束了。

sentences.en: It never went on into 1980, 1981 and so on.
sentences.zh: 它并没有延续到1980年、1981年等等。

sentences.en: I was hugely disappointed about that.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到非常失望。

sentences.en: But what I was thinking now when you were talking about music and the tumultuous events of 81 is the way in which, you know,
sentences.zh: 但刚才当你们在讨论音乐以及81年那些动荡的事件时，我脑子里在想的是，你知道的，

sentences.en: the really scarring experience was, was mass unemployment, inner city deprivation.
sentences.zh: 那种真正留下心理创伤的经历，是，是大规模失业和内城贫困。

sentences.en: And the soundtrack to that you always get is Ghost Town.
sentences.zh: 而你总能听到的与之配套的背景音乐就是《Ghost Town》。

sentences.en: And that's kind of like, you know, the moment you hear that, that, that is early 80s Thatterism.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就像是，你知道的，当你听到这首歌的时候，那就是80年代早期的撒切尔主义。

sentences.en: It's, it just kind of conjures it up, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 它，它就是能勾起那种回忆，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, I did a TV documentary about the 80s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我曾做过一部关于80年代的电视纪录片。

sentences.en: And I can't remember if we used Ghost Town or not.
sentences.zh: 我记不清我们当时有没有用《Ghost Town》这首歌了。

sentences.en: But when we were, we were doing it, we kind of went through and we said, everybody expects it, that when we do the miners strike by law, by sort of UN mandated law,
sentences.zh: 但当我们在，在制作这部片子的时候，我们盘点了一下，然后发现，所有人都有所预期，当我们按法律规定，按某种联合国强制规定的法律去讲矿工大罢工时，

sentences.en: you have to have two tribes, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你肯定得用《Two Tribes》，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: So the footage of the Battle of Orgreave and Two Tribes is playing.
sentences.zh: 所以奥格里夫之战的画面配上《Two Tribes》的音乐正在播放。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And we, we sort of said, we need to steer clear of this as much as we can, although I think we probably did use Ghost Town.
sentences.zh: 然后我们，我们当时就说，我们需要尽可能避开这个，尽管我觉得我们最后可能还是用了《Ghost Town》。

sentences.en: So you're right, that's, but that's true of, I mean, that's true of older periods too, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你是对的，那是，但这也适用于，我的意思是，这也适用于更早的时期，对吧？

sentences.en: That when you're, you're doing mid-Victorian Britain, you always use Dickens.
sentences.zh: 那就是当你研究维多利亚时代中期英国时，你总是会引用狄更斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, but you're talking about music.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我们在谈论音乐。

sentences.en: Music is a kind of lingua franca, if you like.
sentences.zh: 音乐算是一种通用语，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: It's a, everybody understands what it means, everybody has the same associations and so on.
sentences.zh: 它是，每个人都懂它意味着什么，每个人都有相同的联想，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's actually that different from using literary sources from earlier periods to illustrate, you know, to, to sort of connote a particular time,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这其实和使用早期历史时期的文学素材来阐述，你知道的，来，来暗示一个特定的时代，

sentences.en: a particular atmosphere, don't you think?
sentences.zh: 一个特定的氛围，没有什么本质区别，你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's slightly different to the degree that, that music since the fifties has kind of provided a soundtrack that everyone remembers and recognises,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得还是有点区别的，因为五十年代以来的音乐提供了一种人人都记得并能听出来的背景音乐，

sentences.en: simply because the music industry has, has grown so much and the ability of people to consume it has, has, has grown exponentially.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为音乐产业已经，已经发展得如此庞大，人们消费音乐的能力也，也，也呈指数级增长。

sentences.en: And kind of for that reason, it, it, it does kind of conjure up images.
sentences.zh: 而且某种程度上正因如此，它，它，它确实能勾起人们的画面感。

sentences.en: So, so, you know, rather like the Royal Family, Britain has, has been very central to the music industry.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，你知道的，就像皇室一样，英国在音乐产业中一直占据着核心地位。

sentences.en: So I would say that the story of the Beatles is a kind of parallel to the, the story of Diana, that it's,
sentences.zh: 所以我会说披头士乐队的故事某种程度上与戴安娜的故事相似，那就是，

sentences.en: it's a kind of almost mythic tale that everyone kind of instinctively knows.
sentences.zh: 它几乎是一个每个人都凭本能知晓的神话般的故事。

sentences.en: And likewise, the, the story of music, the story of the Royal Family, the story of sport, all of this is a kind of part of the, the, the fabric of recent history.
sentences.zh: 同样地，音乐的故事、皇室的故事、体育的故事，所有这些都是近代历史结构的一部分。

sentences.en: And I just wonder, you know, is it part of that because that's what we remember, that's what we experienced most vividly, or, or is it more significant than that?
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，你知道的，它之所以成为其中的一部分，是因为那是我们所铭记的、我们经历得最深刻的，还是说它有着更重大的意义？

sentences.en: Huh, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 哈，这真是个好问题。

sentences.en: Is it more significant than that?
sentences.zh: 它比这更重大吗？

sentences.en: I think it, it, it, there is a sort of, a story about the, Britain's decline on the world stage and the way we sell ourselves to the world.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它，它，它其中包含着一种关于英国在世界舞台上衰落以及我们向世界兜售自己的方式的故事。

sentences.en: We sell ourselves through pop culture now in a way that we wouldn't have done, you know, in the, let's say the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我们现在通过流行文化来兜售自己，这种方式在，比如说19世纪，是我们不会采用的。

sentences.en: So if you'd said to somebody in 19th century Britain, well, the most important thing about this given moment is our tremendously rich tradition of musical.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你对19世纪英国的某个人说，嗯，当下这个时代最重要的事情是我们极其丰富的音乐传统。

sentences.en: And we will be remembered for our splendid novels.
sentences.zh: 并且我们将因我们灿烂的小说而被人们铭记。

sentences.en: People would have laughed at you.
sentences.zh: 人们会嘲笑你的。

sentences.en: They'd have said that's not important at all.
sentences.zh: 他们会说这根本一点都不重要。

sentences.en: Whereas now I think we do think these things are important and they are redolent of Britishness.
sentences.zh: 然而现在我认为我们确实觉得这些事情很重要，它们充满了英国特色。

sentences.en: So they're what we think matters.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们认为要紧的事情。

sentences.en: So when Danny Boyle did his 2012 Olympics opening ceremony, a lot of it was about Britain's tradition of music and storytelling and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，当丹尼·博伊尔执导2012年伦敦奥运会开幕式时，其中很大一部分内容都是关于英国的音乐和讲故事传统以及其他种种。

sentences.en: That these things were kind of intrinsic to Britishness.
sentences.zh: 这些东西某种程度上是英国特质不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: So it's not surprising that when we tell the story of the very recent past, it's those things that we look to.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们在讲述近代史时，我们会关注这些东西也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Because actually those things seem more sort of vital than, you know, the story of the rise and fall of Ted Heath's government, which most people couldn't give a damn about.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上这些事情看起来比，你知道的，爱德华·希斯政府沉浮的故事要显得更有活力，大多数人根本不在乎后者。

sentences.en: And yet I suppose one of the things about the early 80s is actually that politics is really kind of viscerally in your face in a way that perhaps it hadn't been at any other period.
sentences.zh: 然而我想早期80年代的一个特点其实是，政治以一种或许在任何其他时期都未曾有过的方式，极其直白地扑面而来。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe in the, I don't know, in the Heath government with the three day a week.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许在，我不知道，在希斯政府实行每周三天工作制的时候……

sentences.en: No, he was far more than in the Heath government.
sentences.zh: 不，这比希斯时期强烈得多。

sentences.en: I think politics in the 80s is such a great narrative story.
sentences.zh: 我认为80年代的政治是一个非常棒的故事叙事。

sentences.en: And the divisions in Britain in 81, between north and south, between country and inner city.
sentences.zh: 而且1981年英国的分裂，北方与南方之间，乡村与内城之间。

sentences.en: I mean, give a sense of how divided the country was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这让人感受到这个国家分裂到了什么地步。

sentences.en: I think enormously divided.
sentences.zh: 我认为分裂得极其严重。

sentences.en: And, you know, for people who don't, for younger listeners who don't remember it, Margaret Thatcher had come in in 79 after sort of perceived years of decline.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，对于那些不了解情况的人，对于那些不记得这一切的年轻听众来说，玛格丽特·撒切尔在经历了人们普遍认为的衰退岁月后，于79年上台。

sentences.en: And she basically said she's going to, she was going to administer this shock therapy, this sort of harsh medicine that would turn Britain around.
sentences.zh: 她基本上表示她将，她将实施这种休克疗法，这种能够扭转英国局势的严厉药方。

sentences.en: And after two years, everything seemed to have got incalculably worse.
sentences.zh: 而两年过后，一切似乎都变得无可估量地更糟了。

sentences.en: So Britain was in recession.
sentences.zh: 所以英国陷入了经济衰退。

sentences.en: We had unemployment at more than, you know, heading towards 4 million effectively.
sentences.zh: 我们的失业率超过了，你知道的，实际上正朝着400万逼近。

sentences.en: Young people in particular couldn't get jobs.
sentences.zh: 尤其是年轻人根本找不到工作。

sentences.en: You had riots, first of all, in Brixton in April and then spreading around the country in the summer.
sentences.zh: 先是4月份在布里克斯顿爆发了骚乱，随后在夏天蔓延到全国各地。

sentences.en: You had massive unrest, massive rioting in Northern Ireland where you'd had the hunger strikes of Republican prisoners in the Mays prison.
sentences.zh: 北爱尔兰也爆发了大规模动乱和大规模骚乱，那里曾在梅兹监狱发生过共和党囚犯的绝食抗议。

sentences.en: And you had this sort of sense that the whole country was coming unglued and that almost uniquely in Western Europe, you know, here was this sort of former imperial power,
sentences.zh: 你会有一种整个国家正在四分五裂的感觉，而且在西欧几乎独树一帜的是，你知道的，这里曾是一个老牌帝国主义强国，

sentences.en: this major industrial nation that was just coming apart.
sentences.zh: 这个主要的工业化国家正在分崩离析。

sentences.en: And people were sort of that it was politically tearing itself apart, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得，从政治上讲它正在自我撕裂，我想是这样的。

sentences.en: So the government was the most unpopular government since records began.
sentences.zh: 所以该政府是有记录以来最不受欢迎的政府。

sentences.en: The Labour Party, the opposition party was incredibly bitterly divided.
sentences.zh: 工党，也就是反对党，内部的分歧极其严重和痛苦。

sentences.en: And there was this real sense of, which far greater, I think, than anything even over Brexit, of rancor and of sort of, you know, hostility.
sentences.zh: 这种强烈的怨恨和敌意感，我认为甚至远远超过了脱欧时期的任何状况。

sentences.en: A real sense of the stakes being so high and the stakes being the survivor of the United Kingdom, you know, the prosperity of you and your family.
sentences.zh: 那种孤注一掷的真实感，赌注是联合王国的生存，你知道的，是你和你家人的繁荣。

sentences.en: You know, this is not a sort of, these are not symbolic issues.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这可不是一种，这些可不是象征性的问题。

sentences.en: These are incredibly visceral kind of bread and butter issues.
sentences.zh: 这些是极其直观的、关乎生计的硬核问题。

sentences.en: But you see, the reason why recent history is, I find it kind of challenging to get a handle on, is that I lived through it.
sentences.zh: 但你看，为什么近代历史让我觉得很难摸透，原因在于我亲历了那个时期。

sentences.en: And I was in a idyllic Wiltshire village.
sentences.zh: 当时我身处威尔特郡的一个田园诗般的村庄里。

sentences.en: And oddly, I now live in Brixton.
sentences.zh: 而奇怪的是，我现在住在布里克斯顿。

sentences.en: So, you know, and Brixton was kind of the epicentre of police brutality and the rioting.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，布里克斯顿曾是警察暴行和骚乱的震中。

sentences.en: But, you know, it was, it was, it might as well have been a million miles from me.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，它当时，它当时对我和远在天边没什么两样。

sentences.en: And what I remember about the summer of 81 is that my mother was in hospital.
sentences.zh: 我对1981年夏天的记忆是，我母亲当时在住院。

sentences.en: My father said, you know, he had to look after me, didn't he, what else to do?
sentences.zh: 我父亲说，你知道的，他不得不照顾我，不是吗？还能怎么办？

sentences.en: He said, well, let's watch a test match.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，我们来看一场板球对抗赛吧。

sentences.en: And I had no interest in cricket, had no interest in sport at all.
sentences.zh: 我对板球毫无兴趣，对体育运动根本一点兴趣都没有。

sentences.en: That test match was headingly, and it was one of the most transformative, remarkable cricket matches of all time.
sentences.zh: 那场对抗赛是在海丁利球馆举行的，它是史上最具颠覆性、最卓越的板球比赛之一。

sentences.en: I know that people who are not interested in cricket, certainly people who are not British listening to this will be slightly bewildered by it.
sentences.zh: 我知道那些对板球不感兴趣的人，尤其是听到这里的非英国听众，会对这一点感到有些迷惑不解。

sentences.en: But there was this astonishing kind of fairytale reversal where England had been down and out.
sentences.zh: 但当时出现了那种令人惊叹的、像童话般的惊天大逆转，原本处于绝境的英格兰队绝地反击。

sentences.en: They triumphed against all the odds over Australia, our old sporting rival.
sentences.zh: 他们克服重重困难，战胜了我们老牌的体育宿敌澳大利亚队。

sentences.en: And Ian Botham, a figure who is now famous chiefly for supporting Brexit and having been raised by Boris Johnson to the House of Lords, was the hero of the hour.
sentences.zh: 而伊恩·博瑟姆——如今主要因支持脱欧以及被鲍里斯·约翰逊擢升为上议院议员而闻名的人物——成了当之无愧的英雄。

sentences.en: And that essentially changed my life because it persuaded me to take off cricket, which has been one of the great loves of my life ever since.
sentences.zh: 这基本上改变了我的人生，因为它说服我迷上了板球，板球自此成为我一生中最大的挚爱之一。

sentences.en: So that is how I remember 1981.
sentences.zh: 这就是我记忆中的1981年。

sentences.en: So emotionally, personally, that's my stake in it.
sentences.zh: 所以在情感上、个人层面上，这就是我与那段历史的联结。

sentences.en: I had no personal experience of riots or unemployment or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我对骚乱、失业或诸如此类的事情没有任何个人经历。

sentences.en: And it's kind of, you know, it makes sense of what's often said about the great events is that actually, and it's a point you make repeatedly throughout your books,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这印证了人们对重大历史事件的常见说法，并且这也是你在书中多次阐述的一个观点，

sentences.en: that often, even when terrible things are happening, most people are actually perfectly happy.
sentences.zh: 那就是通常情况下，即便可怕的事情正在发生，大多数人其实也过得十分快乐。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想你说得对，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, I think we should get onto the cricket in a second.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得我们一会儿得聊聊板球了。

sentences.en: I can't believe, by the way, it took you more than 15 minutes of this podcast to turn the conversation to Ian Botham.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我简直不敢相信，在这期播客里你花了超过15分钟才把话题引到伊恩·博瑟姆身上。

sentences.en: However, let's put Botham on one side.
sentences.zh: 不过，咱们先暂且把博瑟姆搁在一边。

sentences.en: Let's come back to Botham and the cricket because I think the cricket actually does have a proper historical significance, which we can get into maybe after the break.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到博瑟姆和板球的话题上来，因为我认为板球实际上确实具有真正的历史意义，也许我们可以在中场休息后深入探讨。

sentences.en: But before that, yes, it's a very strange thing writing about contemporary history because, of course, often when you're talking about it,
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，是的，撰写当代史是一件非常奇怪的事情，因为当然，当你谈论它的时候，

sentences.en: you're talking to people who live through it.
sentences.zh: 你通常是在跟那些亲历过那个时代的人对话。

sentences.en: Now, that's not a problem that you really have when you're doing, you know, Dynasty or Rubicon or any of your books on the Romans or the Greeks or whatever.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是你在写，你知道的，《王朝》、《卢比孔河》或你任何关于罗马人、希腊人或诸如此类的书时真正需要面对的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, they're not around to tell you you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们可不在世来告诉你你写错了。

sentences.en: When I go to talk about my books, often, you know, there'll be people nodding in the audience and then there'll be other people who say,
sentences.zh: 当我去做关于我的书的讲座时，通常，你知道的，听众席上会有人点头，然后还会有另一些人说，

sentences.en: oh, but the 60s wasn't like that at all or the 70s, you know, wasn't like that.
sentences.zh: 哦，但60年代根本不是那样的，或者说70年代，你知道的，根本不是那个样子的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's very common.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常普遍。

sentences.en: And I guess one of the things with being a historian of contemporary Britain is, first of all, you have to put your own experience on one side.
sentences.zh: 我想作为当代英国的历史学家，其中一件事就是，首先，你必须把自己的个人经历放在一边。

sentences.en: But also you have to juggle, you know, your own job as the historian, which is to impose your pattern and to tell your story.
sentences.zh: 但同时你也必须兼顾，你知道的，你作为历史学家的本职工作，也就是构建你的叙事结构并讲述你的故事。

sentences.en: But also the complexity of all these kind of individual stories.
sentences.zh: 以及所有这些形形色色个人故事的复杂性。

sentences.en: Now, that's not really something that you have to confront as an ancient historian because you don't have many sources.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这并不是你在作为古代历史学家时需要去面对的事情，因为你并没有那么多的史料。

sentences.en: So you don't have all the individual stories of all the people who are unrepresentative.
sentences.zh: 所以你不会拥有所有那些缺乏代表性的普通人的个人故事。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But I think that one of the fascinating things about ancient history often is the glimpses you get occasionally of people leading their normal lives.
sentences.zh: 但我认为古代历史最迷人的地方之一，往往在于你能偶尔一窥人们过着他们平常生活的场景。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it could be preserved on tombstones.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会被保存在墓碑上。

sentences.en: It could be preserved in a poem.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会被保存在一首诗里。

sentences.en: You know, the hints of what it's like to just go out and lie in a field while civil war is going on all around you.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种仅仅是走出去，躺在田野里，而内战就在你身边各处发生时的生活微末感受。

sentences.en: Give us an example.
sentences.zh: 给我们举个例子。

sentences.en: Well, actually, the example that always sticks in my mind comes from the letters of Cicero.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，一直留在我脑海里的例子出自西塞罗的书信。

sentences.en: Cicero, of course, is intimately involved in the convulsions that ends the Roman Republic.
sentences.zh: 西塞罗，当然，深度参与了终结罗马共和国的动乱。

sentences.en: But there's a letter in which he writes about a house he owns and it's got a crack.
sentences.zh: 但有一封信里他写到了自己拥有的一栋房子，而且房子裂了一条缝。

sentences.en: You know, a crack has opened up and he's a bit worried about this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，裂开了一条缝，他对此有点担心。

sentences.en: You know, how are you going to repair it?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你该怎么去修补它呢？

sentences.en: And the idea that even amid all the events that Cicero was intimately involved in, he's worrying about kind of DIY repairs and things like that.
sentences.zh: 这种想法是，即便在西塞罗深陷其中的所有重大事件之中，他还在担心诸如DIY房屋修缮之类的事情。

sentences.en: What's he going to do?
sentences.zh: 他该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: I think that that's expressive of a fundamental truth that life carries on.
sentences.zh: 我认为这表达了一个基本真理，那就是生活仍在继续。

sentences.en: It goes on.
sentences.zh: 它在向前走。

sentences.en: There's kind of famous Hardy poem, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 有一种很著名的托马斯·哈代写的诗，对吧？

sentences.en: Which I think he wrote where he says, do you know what?
sentences.zh: 我想那是他写的，里面写道，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Let's let's go for a break and I'll look that that Hardy poem up and I'll read it to you when we come back.
sentences.zh: 咱们，咱们休息一会儿，我去把那首哈代写的诗找出来，等我们回来后读给你听。

sentences.en: Welcome back, everybody.
sentences.zh: 欢迎大家回来。

sentences.en: I think Tom has a poem for us.
sentences.zh: 我想汤姆有一首诗要送给我们。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我确实有。

sentences.en: It's the first poem that we've had on The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在《历史其余部分》节目中录入的第一首诗。

sentences.en: It's by Hardy and it's called In Time of the Breaking of Nations.
sentences.zh: 它是哈代写的，名叫《在摧毁国家之时》。

sentences.en: I'm going to read the third verse.
sentences.zh: 我来朗读第三节。

sentences.en: And it's yonder a maid and her white come whispering by.
sentences.zh: 那边一个姑娘和她身穿白衣的情郎低语着走过。

sentences.en: War's annals will cloud into night ere their story die.
sentences.zh: 在他们的故事消逝前，战争的编年史早已隐入黑夜。

sentences.en: So, you know, girls and boys will hang out with each other, even though war's going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，少男少女们依然会聚在一起，尽管战争正在进行。

sentences.en: But interestingly, the first verse, only a man harrowing clods in a slow, silent walk with an old horse that stumbles and nods half asleep as they stalk.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是第一节，只有一个人迈着缓慢、沉默的步伐在翻耕泥土，身旁是一匹老马，它一颠一颠地打着半瞌睡，一边前行。

sentences.en: So, Hardy's saying, you know, that people will be ploughing with horses till the end of time.
sentences.zh: 所以，哈代是在说，你知道的，人们会一直用马犁地直到时间的尽头。

sentences.en: And that obviously isn't true.
sentences.zh: 而这显然不是真的。

sentences.en: So, things do change.
sentences.zh: 所以，事物确实在变。

sentences.en: Lots of good examples like this, aren't there, Tom?
sentences.zh: 有很多像这样的好例子，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: I was thinking one before, just before the break.
sentences.zh: 我之前想过一个，就在中场休息前。

sentences.en: So, the only source from the day that Alexander the Great died was a Babylonian astrological diary kept by a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚历山大大帝去世那天唯一的记载来源是一份由一位祭司保存的巴比伦占星日记。

sentences.en: And it's all about the weather.
sentences.zh: 上面写满了关于天气的内容。

sentences.en: So, he sort of says, the king died.
sentences.zh: 所以他大概是这么写的，国王驾崩了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, it was very cloudy and overcast and bloody.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，天气非常多云、阴暗且该死的糟糕。

sentences.en: And he gives more attention to the weather than he does.
sentences.zh: 比起其他事，他对天气的关注要多得多。

sentences.en: And that's how most of us think about politics and, you know, the world, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而这不正是我们大多数人思考政治和，你知道的，世界的方式吗？

sentences.en: It's apocryphal, isn't it, that on the 14th of July, Louis XVI's diary read, nothing much happened.
sentences.zh: 这是一个戏说，对吧，据说在7月14日那天，路易十六的日记里写着：今天没什么大事发生。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that probably is.
sentences.zh: 对，我想那很可能就是真的。

sentences.en: I think it was, maybe it was the record of game or something.
sentences.zh: 我想是的，也许那是比赛记录什么的。

sentences.en: I think that's what all kings post about 1700 are supposed to have written about major events.
sentences.zh: 我想1700年以后所有国王的帖子，大概都是写重大事件的。

sentences.en: Anyway, back to 81.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，回到81年。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You were going to say that actually the cricket in 1981 was of immense historical significance, which I'd love to be reassured on that because that would be great to learn.
sentences.zh: 你刚才本来要说，实际上1981年的板球运动具有巨大的历史意义，我很希望得到这方面的证实，因为了解这些会很棒。

sentences.en: I think it is of great historical significance.
sentences.zh: 我认为它具有重大的历史意义。

sentences.en: So, the news for Britain since the late 60s had been pretty awful.
sentences.zh: 所以，自60年代末以来，英国的种种消息一直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: So, although most people are actually better off than they'd ever been, the sort of headlines were always bad.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管大多数人的生活实际上比以往任何时候都好，但头条新闻总是很糟糕。

sentences.en: So, from about 1967 onwards, which is when Harold Wilson devalued the pound,
sentences.zh: 因此，从1967年左右开始，也就是哈罗德·威尔逊将英镑贬值的时候，

sentences.en: governments had been constantly in trouble and everything had been bad for Britain.
sentences.zh: 各届政府一直陷入麻烦，英国的一切都很糟糕。

sentences.en: And I think at the end of the 1970s, you started to get this sense that people were thirsting for some good news.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在70年代末，你开始感觉到人们渴望听到一些好消息。

sentences.en: So, the first sign of that, I think, was the reaction to the SAS's raid on the Iranian embassy, which they liberated from a siege in 1980.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这方面的第一个迹象，是人们对特种空勤团突袭伊朗大使馆行动的反应，他们在1980年的围困中解放了大使馆。

sentences.en: And you have this almost hysterical reaction from the tabloids and so on, that Britain is great again, we're top nation, all of this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 小报等媒体对此做出了近乎歇斯底里的反应，说什么英国再次伟大、我们是顶级国家之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then you see it again twice in 1981.
sentences.zh: 然后你在1981年又两次看到了这种现象。

sentences.en: Once is the royal wedding, when, you know, we lead the world in pomp and pageantry.
sentences.zh: 一次是皇家婚礼，当时，你知道，我们在浮华和盛典方面引领世界。

sentences.en: And the other time is this incredibly hysterical reaction to winning one test match.
sentences.zh: 另一次是对赢得一场测试赛的这种难以置信的歇斯底里反应。

sentences.en: No, three.
sentences.zh: 不，三场。

sentences.en: We won three.
sentences.zh: 我们赢了三场。

sentences.en: We won three.
sentences.zh: 我们赢了三场。

sentences.en: Yes, but it's the Hellingley test that sparks the reaction.
sentences.zh: 是的，但引发这种反应的是海林格测试赛。

sentences.en: Yes, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: So, it's the comeback.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是卷土重来。

sentences.en: And I think the funny thing about it is, so, Botham, who is the hero of the hour, he had been the England captain.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得有趣的是，博瑟姆作为当时的英雄，他曾担任过英格兰队长。

sentences.en: He'd been this incredibly sort of youthful figure, this sort of raging lion, who's carrying all before him, who's appointed England captain.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一个极其年轻的人物，就像一头咆哮的狮子，横扫一切，被任命为英格兰队长。

sentences.en: And then he doesn't win a match as captain.
sentences.zh: 然后他作为队长却没有赢下一场比赛。

sentences.en: He has the worst record of any test captain at that point in history.
sentences.zh: 他是那段历史中战绩最差的测试赛队长。

sentences.en: And he's sacked from the captaincy.
sentences.zh: 然后他被解除了队长职务。

sentences.en: And the day that he's sacked from the captaincy, the headlines are juxtaposed with the images of rioting.
sentences.zh: 在他被解除队长职务的那天，头条新闻与骚乱的画面并列出现。

sentences.en: So, they're the two main stories.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是两个主要故事。

sentences.en: And they're both basically the same story.
sentences.zh: 而且它们基本上是同一个故事。

sentences.en: And that story is, Britain has been great, but now it's rubbish.
sentences.zh: 那个故事就是，英国曾经很伟大，但现在一团糟。

sentences.en: It's tearing itself apart.
sentences.zh: 它正在自我撕裂。

sentences.en: It can't win cricket matches.
sentences.zh: 它赢不了板球比赛。

sentences.en: Its cities are in flames.
sentences.zh: 它的城市陷入火海。

sentences.en: All is sort of disaster.
sentences.zh: 到处都是灾难。

sentences.en: And then, Botham, of all people, the sort of incarnation of conservative, working-class England, turns it around, doesn't he, in this extraordinary sort of Herculean feat.
sentences.zh: 然后，偏偏是博瑟姆，这个保守的英国工人阶级的化身，通过这种非凡的、类似海格力斯的壮举扭转了局面，不是吗？

sentences.en: And the press are beside themselves.
sentences.zh: 媒体欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: We are top nation again.
sentences.zh: 我们又成了顶级国家。

sentences.en: And then just a couple of weeks later, you have the royal wedding.
sentences.zh: 紧接着几周后，就迎来了皇家婚礼。

sentences.en: And, of course, what that all lays the foundation for, I think, is the sort of populist patriotism that you get with the Falklands.
sentences.zh: 当然，我认为这一切为马岛战争中那种民粹主义爱国主义奠定了基础。

sentences.en: So, it's basically laying, you know, these are all omens of what is to come a year later when the Falklands War happens.
sentences.zh: 所以，这基本上是在铺垫，你知道，这些都是一年后马岛战争爆发时的预兆。

sentences.en: And these are elements of what you'd call Thatcherism, of Thatcher's sort of, you know, nationwide appeal to a particular audience, which Botham still incarnates.
sentences.zh: 这些也就是你所谓的撒切尔主义的元素，是撒切尔对特定受众的全国性号召力，博瑟姆至今仍是这种号召力的化身。

sentences.en: Well, it's often said of the Players' Association, which is the trades union of professional cricketers, that it's the only trades union that's more right-wing than its employers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，人们常说球员协会（职业板球运动员的工会）是唯一一个比其雇主还要右翼的工会。

sentences.en: And, I mean, Botham becomes a kind of emblem for the triumph of Thatcherite, well, England, really, rather than Britain, Thatcherite England.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，博瑟姆成了撒切尔主义胜利的某种象征，与其说是英国，不如说是撒切尔主义的英格兰。

sentences.en: He's a hunting, shooting, fishing man, and in due course he becomes a Brexiteer, and he's now in the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 他是一个热衷打猎、射击、钓鱼的人，后来他成了脱欧派，现在他在上议院。

sentences.en: Well, what's so interesting about him, right, is that he's forward-looking and backward-looking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于他最有趣的是，对吧，他既有前瞻性又有复古情怀。

sentences.en: So, if you take Ian Botham in 1981,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你以1981年的伊恩·博瑟姆为例，

sentences.en: he, you know, you can sort of look forward and say Brexit and all of that kind of stuff, or you can look back and you can say he's basically,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以展望未来并说脱欧之类的事情，或者你可以回溯过去并说他基本上是，

sentences.en: what is he, an 18th century figure?
sentences.zh: 他是什么，一个18世纪的人物吗？

sentences.en: You know, you can imagine him on the deck of HMS Victory, you know, the roast beef of old England.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以想象他在胜利号战舰的甲板上，你知道，那是老英格兰的烤牛肉。

sentences.en: I mean, his very nickname, Beefy, could not be more 18th century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的绰号“壮汉”（Beefy），再具有18世纪的特色不过了。

sentences.en: And there was a very embarrassing stage where he went to L.A.
sentences.zh: 曾有过一个非常尴尬的阶段，他去洛杉矶试图扮演詹姆斯·邦德，我想我们就对这一幕闭口不谈吧。

sentences.en: to try and become James Bond, which I think will draw a curtain over that.
sentences.zh: 但我不想多说那个。

sentences.en: But there is also another aspect to Botham, which ties in, interestingly, with particularly the race riots, is that Botham was great friends with Viv Richards,
sentences.zh: 但博瑟姆还有另一个方面，有趣的是，它与种族骚乱紧密相连，那就是博瑟姆和维夫·理查兹是好朋友，

sentences.en: probably the great West Indies batsman, the greatest batsman of his day.
sentences.zh: 后者可能是西印度群岛最伟大的击球手，他那个时代最伟大的击球手。

sentences.en: Botham was always slightly in his shadow.
sentences.zh: 博瑟姆总是略微生活在他的阴影下。

sentences.en: And interestingly, another thing, kind of, you know, looking forward to 2020, is that the trophy that West Indies and England compete for,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，还有一件事，有点像，你知道的，展望2020年，西印度群岛和英格兰争夺的奖杯，

sentences.en: had been called the Wisdom Trophy, is now the Viv Richards, Ian Botham Trophy.
sentences.zh: 以前被称为“威斯登奖杯”，现在是“维夫·理查兹-伊恩·博瑟姆奖杯”。

sentences.en: So there is also a sense in which he's looking forward to a future in which race relations will be less explosive than they were in 1981.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某种意义上，他也正展望着一个种族关系没有1981年那么剑拔弩张的未来。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a really interesting point.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常有趣的观点。

sentences.en: And I think one reason that he got on so well with Viv Richards was they were both outsiders.
sentences.zh: 我想他和维夫·理查兹相处得那么好，原因之一是他们都是局外人。

sentences.en: And Botham felt very keenly his outsider status in a game dominated by white public schoolboys.
sentences.zh: 博瑟姆深刻地感受到了自己在由白人公学男孩主导的运动中的局外人身份。

sentences.en: So he sort of, he bonded with Viv Richards, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他某种程度上与维夫·理查兹建立了羁绊，对吧？

sentences.en: I think he wore the Jamaican colours in a kind of wristband to show his solidarity with Richards.
sentences.zh: 我想他戴着牙买加颜色的腕带，以示对理查兹的支持。

sentences.en: And that's really interesting because you have this sort of almost like black and white alliance of the outsiders against the old guard, the Toffs,
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为你看到了这种黑白联盟，局外人对抗老卫队、贵族阶层，

sentences.en: that Botham and Richards felt were dominating the game.
sentences.zh: 博瑟姆和理查兹觉得这些人统治了这项运动。

sentences.en: OK, and so that's the kind of thing that a historian would do, is to pick up on a totemic figure like that and tease out aspects of him
sentences.zh: 好的，历史学家通常会这样做，就是挑选一个具有图腾色彩的人物，并剥茧抽丝出他身上的某些方面，

sentences.en: that perhaps you could then feed back into the broader context.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以将这些方面反馈到更广泛的背景中。

sentences.en: Is that a fair thing to do?
sentences.zh: 这样做公平吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if we're looking at the Royal Wedding, we're looking at the cricket, we're looking at the music.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我们看看皇家婚礼，看看板球，看看音乐。

sentences.en: What does that tell us about trade union policy of the Thatcher government?
sentences.zh: 这向我们透露了关于撒切尔政府工会政策的什么信息？

sentences.en: Answer me that.
sentences.zh: 回答我这个。

sentences.en: OK, you've sent me a challenge here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你在这里给我出了个难题。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, my answer to that would be that Thatcher's trade union policy succeeded because most ordinary trade unionists generally agreed with the piecemeal bits of the...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的回答是，撒切尔的工会政策之所以成功，是因为大多数普通工会成员普遍赞同那些零碎的……

sentences.en: So each individual reform that she passed, individual trade unionists agreed with.
sentences.zh: 所以她通过的每一项具体改革，个别工会成员都是赞同的。

sentences.en: Their leaders didn't agree with them.
sentences.zh: 他们的领导人并不赞同。

sentences.en: But she obviously appealed to a kind of aspirational, working class, you know, sort of skilled, respectable, upwardly mobile working class people, particularly in England.
sentences.zh: 但她显然吸引了一种具有进取心的、工阶层的、你知道的、有技能的、受人尊敬的、渴望向上流动的工阶层群体，特别是在英格兰。

sentences.en: So your classic kind of Essex man.
sentences.zh: 所以你典型的埃塞克斯人那种。

sentences.en: Now, Ian Botham is not an Essex man, but there are definitely parallels.
sentences.zh: 现在，伊恩·博瑟姆不是埃塞克斯人，但两者肯定有相似之处。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of working class conservatism that Thatcher's union policy reaches out to, which is, you know, your union is actually...
sentences.zh: 撒切尔的工会政策触及了一种工阶层的保守主义，那就是，你知道的，你的工会实际上是在……

sentences.en: She says your union is holding you back.
sentences.zh: 她说你的工会正在拖累你。

sentences.en: Your collective loyalty is holding you back.
sentences.zh: 你的集体忠诚正在拖累你。

sentences.en: You should think of yourself as an individual and get on and fight for a better life.
sentences.zh: 你应该把自己当成一个独立的个体去奋斗，去争取更好的生活。

sentences.en: That's what Ian Botham's about, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是伊恩·博瑟姆所代表的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so opinions on, moving on from both of them, I mean, actually opinions on both of them, but opinions on the Thatcher government and perhaps Mrs. Thatcher particularly,
sentences.zh: 接着从这两者继续说下去，关于他们的看法，实际上对他们两人的看法，还有对撒切尔政府以及也许特别是撒切尔夫人的看法，

sentences.en: it's a subject of history, but it still remains very, very intensely a matter of politics as well.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是一个历史课题，而且在今天依然是一个非常、非常强烈的政治问题。

sentences.en: Your opinion of what Mrs. Thatcher did will define you politically today in 2020.
sentences.zh: 你在2020年对撒切尔夫人所作所为的看法，将定义你的政治立场。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，汤姆。

sentences.en: You know, in a sense, you know, like the French Revolution, it's too early to tell.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在某种意义上，就像法国大革命一样，现在下结论还为时过早。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对此并不确定。

sentences.en: It's too early to tell.
sentences.zh: 现在下结论还为时过早。

sentences.en: I'll tell you what story.
sentences.zh: 我给你讲个故事。

sentences.en: I was, when I first decided I was going to write these series of books about modern Britain, a friend of mine who's now a professor of history at Leeds, he said to me,
sentences.zh: 当我最初决定要写这套关于现代英国的书时，我的一个朋友现在是利兹大学的历史学教授，他跟我说，

sentences.en: are you going to do the 80s?
sentences.zh: 你打算写80年代吗？

sentences.en: And I said, oh, yeah, I have to.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，是的，我必须写。

sentences.en: And he said, what, are you going to do Thatcher?
sentences.zh: 他说，什么，你打算写撒切尔？

sentences.en: I said, yeah, yeah, well, and he just kind of laughed in quite a sort of mocking way.
sentences.zh: 我说，对，对，嗯，然后他带着一种嘲讽的语气笑了笑。

sentences.en: And he said, everybody will really hate you, you know.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，所有人都会真的很讨厌你。

sentences.en: And I said, why?
sentences.zh: 我说，为什么？

sentences.en: He said, well, because I know you.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，因为我了解你。

sentences.en: You're trying to find, you know, you'll see both sides.
sentences.zh: 你总是试图去寻找，你知道的，你会看到双方的观点。

sentences.en: You'll try to be balanced and all this.
sentences.zh: 你会试图保持平衡之类的。

sentences.en: You can't be balanced about Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 关于撒切尔，你没办法保持平衡。

sentences.en: People just want you to hate her.
sentences.zh: 人们只想让你讨厌她。

sentences.en: And, of course, there's some truth in that.
sentences.zh: 当然，这其中有一定道理。

sentences.en: And my way of dealing with that partly was to say, of Thatcher, you know, in some ways, she's the last sort of great man.
sentences.zh: 我部分应对这一点的方式是，对于撒切尔，你知道的，在某些方面，她是最后一位所谓的大人物。

sentences.en: We talked about greatness in the first episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一集里谈论过伟大人物。

sentences.en: Great man, great woman, sort of historiographical subject left.
sentences.zh: 大人物，伟大女性，这是历史编纂学留下的主题。

sentences.en: So people base it.
sentences.zh: 所以人们以此为基础。

sentences.en: Their attitude to Thatcher is they think she changed Britain, either for good or ill.
sentences.zh: 他们对撒切尔的态度是，他们认为她改变了英国，无论是变好还是变坏。

sentences.en: And one of my big arguments is, actually, you know, is that really true?
sentences.zh: 我的主要论点之一其实是，你知道的，这真的是真的吗？

sentences.en: Or is she really reflecting changes that are driven from below, as it were?
sentences.zh: 还是说她其实只是反映了从底层（可以说是自下而上）推动的变化？

sentences.en: You know, if she died in 1978, would Britain have been very different?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果她在1978年去世，英国会有很大不同吗？

sentences.en: My argument is that it wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是不会。

sentences.en: That what happened actually happened.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情终究会发生。

sentences.en: You know, she was a symptom of the change rather than the cause of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她更多是这种变化的症状，而不是它的原因。

sentences.en: So actually, it doesn't matter whether you think she was brilliant or terrible.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，你觉得她绝顶聪明还是糟糕透顶都无所谓。

sentences.en: Because one of the arguments about what's happening at the moment with COVID and the way that it's affecting the north of England much worse than the south
sentences.zh: 因为关于目前新冠疫情以及它对英格兰北部的打击远重于南部这一现象的辩驳之一是，

sentences.en: is that this reflects kind of deep, deep, deep-rooted trends for which Mrs. Thatcher is held responsible.
sentences.zh: 这反映了某种根深蒂固的趋势，而撒切尔夫人被认为应当为此负责。

sentences.en: The kind of, the destruction of heavy industry mining and so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如重工业、采矿业的毁灭等等。

sentences.en: Do you think that there is, I mean, can we trace the threads of what happened in the 80s through to the incidence rates of infection and COVID?
sentences.zh: 你认为，我的意思是，我们能否将80年代发生的事情的脉络追溯到感染率和新冠疫情上？

sentences.en: Or is that, or does that remain a kind of political rather than a historical judgment?
sentences.zh: 还是说，这依然是一种政治判断而非历史判断？

sentences.en: I think that is a political judgment, actually, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为这实际上是一种政治判断。

sentences.en: And two things occurred to me about that.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我有两点想法。

sentences.en: One is, first of all, there'd been a big divergence between north and south.
sentences.zh: 首先，南北之间早就存在巨大的分歧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Long before that.
sentences.zh: 那是在很久以前。

sentences.en: I mean, I know you're a big fan of that book by Dan Jackson, The Northumbrians.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道你是丹·杰克逊那本《诺森布里亚人》的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that really, I mean, you look at books like that, that really brings alive just how different the north, the experience in the north of England felt for hundreds of years
sentences.zh: 真的，我的意思是，你看这样的书，它真的生动地展现了数百年来英格兰北部的经历有多么不同，

sentences.en: from the experience in the south.
sentences.zh: 与南部的经历截然不同。

sentences.en: You know, they're not, they were two nations, as it were, long before Margaret Thatcher had been a glint in Alderman Roberts' eye.
sentences.zh: 你知道，早在玛格丽特·撒切尔还在阿尔德曼·罗伯茨的脑海中闪现之前，它们就已经像是两个国家了。

sentences.en: And so your perspective is basically the Marxist one, that these are deep-rooted issues that are, you know, these are the great surging waves of history,
sentences.zh: 所以你的视角基本上是马克思主义的视角，即这些都是根深蒂固的问题，你知道的，这些是历史的滔滔巨浪，

sentences.en: and that someone like Mrs Thatcher is just the kind of, the foam on the crest of the wave.
sentences.zh: 而像撒切尔夫人这样的人只是浪尖上的泡沫。

sentences.en: That is exactly my position, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这完全就是我的立场。

sentences.en: And I'll give you an example of that.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: You talked about the death of heavy industry.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了重工业的消亡。

sentences.en: Does anybody seriously think that without Margaret Thatcher, you know, tens, if not hundreds of thousands of people would every morning be going down pits to dig for coal?
sentences.zh: 难道真有人认为，如果没有玛格丽特·撒切尔，你知道的，成千上万甚至数十万人每天早晨还会下井去挖煤吗？

sentences.en: I mean, all that heavy industry has died in every other Europe, virtually every other European country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些重工业在欧洲其他所有国家（几乎所有其他欧洲国家）都消亡了。

sentences.en: So the idea that it's all Margaret Thatcher's fault and it would happen, I mean, it might have happened more slowly, it might have happened less contentiously,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果认为这全都是玛格丽特·撒切尔的错，而且本来可以避免，我的意思是，它可能会发生得更慢一些，可能会不那么饱受争议，

sentences.en: it might have happened, you know, things might have worked out differently, but the basic story would still have been the same.
sentences.zh: 它可能会发生，你知道的，事情可能会有不同的发展，但基本的故事仍会是一样的。

sentences.en: So in that sense, yes, that is kind of Marxist history, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，是的，这有点像马克思主义的历史观，不是吗？

sentences.en: Great big forces and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 宏大的历史力量以及其他种种。

sentences.en: To hold this kind of demonic status or, you know, status of heroin, depending on which side of the debate you stand.
sentences.zh: 取决于你站在辩论的哪一边，她被赋予了某种恶魔般的地位，或者说英雄般的地位。

sentences.en: Because I remember there was some, was it last year, maybe the year before, there was a really excellent series on the BBC about Mrs Thatcher, which was...
sentences.zh: 因为我记得有一些，是去年吗，也许是前年，BBC上有一部关于撒切尔夫人的非常优秀的系列片，那是……

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm so glad you mentioned that, Tom, because I was the consultant for that series.
sentences.zh: 是的，汤姆，我很高兴你提到这个，因为我是那个系列片的顾问。

sentences.en: Okay, well, it was, I thought, oh, Dominic, well, it was really excellent.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我觉得，哦，多米尼克，真的非常棒。

sentences.en: I think, and I think it didn't have any commentary at all, did it?
sentences.zh: 我想，而且我觉得它完全没有任何旁白，对吧？

sentences.en: It was just kind of...
sentences.zh: 它只是一种……

sentences.en: No, no presenter, no commentary, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有主持人，没有解说，对。

sentences.en: Contemporary footage and interviewees.
sentences.zh: 有当时的影像资料和受访者。

sentences.en: And I watched that with my daughter, who must have been, I don't know, 16 at the time or something, knew nothing about the subject at all.
sentences.zh: 我跟我女儿一起看的，她当时大概，我不知道，16岁左右吧，对这个话题完全一无所知。

sentences.en: And her take on it was very much that of a kind of young feminiSt.
sentences.zh: 而她对这件事的看法非常像那种年轻的女权主义者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That she was watching a woman triumphing over these kind of chauvinist dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 她看到的是一个女性在战胜这些大男子主义老古董。

sentences.en: And that was her take.
sentences.zh: 这就是她的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that story, that side of it, will definitely come out.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得那个故事，那方面的内容，肯定会表现出来。

sentences.en: That, you know, people will see her as a working woman surrounded by men in a way that they didn't, you know, 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 也就是，你知道的，人们会把她看作一个被男人包围的职场女性，这种视角在20年前是没有的。

sentences.en: They didn't see the femininity of Margaret Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 他们当时没有看到玛格丽特·撒切尔身上的女性特质。

sentences.en: Or indeed, they said she's not really a woman at all, which nobody really would say now.
sentences.zh: 或者干脆说，他们觉得她根本算不上女人，这种话现在谁也不会说了。

sentences.en: I can see that even as I'm speaking, the producer is throwing texts at me that say, she didn't like women, she didn't champion women, and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我能看出来，就在我说话的时候，制作人一直在给我发信息说，她不喜欢女人，她不为女性发声，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: But in that respect, actually,
sentences.zh: 但从这方面来讲，实际上，

sentences.en: Margaret Thatcher was typical of women of her type.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特·撒切尔跟她那类女性很典型。

sentences.en: People used to talk at the time about queen bees, about women who had got ahead in the 60s and 70s and then didn't pull up other women after them.
sentences.zh: 当时人们经常谈论“女王蜂”，谈论那些在60和70年代出人头地，却没有提携后辈女性的女性。

sentences.en: And psychologically, actually, you can sort of understand why some women behave like that.
sentences.zh: 而且从心理学上讲，其实，你大概能理解为什么有些女性会那样做。

sentences.en: They thought, like Margaret Thatcher thought, well, I've got ahead on my own merits.
sentences.zh: 她们觉得，就像玛格丽特·撒切尔想的那样，嗯，我是凭自己的本事出人头地的。

sentences.en: Why should I, you know,
sentences.zh: 凭什么让我，你知道的，

sentences.en: institute affirmative action for other women?
sentences.zh: 为其他女性制定平权行动？

sentences.en: They should work just like I've worked.
sentences.zh: 她们应该像我一样努力工作才对。

sentences.en: And there was always this tension between those women who'd been the first ones to get ahead, the kind of professional women,
sentences.zh: 在那些第一批出人头地的女性——也就是那类职业女性——与后来者之间，一直存在着这种紧张关系。

sentences.en: those who came after them.
sentences.zh: 不过你说得对。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们会，我是说年轻人，年轻人根本不在乎，对吧？

sentences.en: I think people will, younger people, I mean, younger people won't care, will they?
sentences.zh: 在10年或20年后，他们会在乎马岛战争和矿工罢工吗？

sentences.en: In 10 or 20 years time, will they care about the Falklands and the minor strikes?
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过我觉得我女儿对那个故事本身的反应——在完全不懂更广阔政治背景的情况下——再次说明了，

sentences.en: Well, but I think that what my daughter's response to just to that story, having no sense of the broader politics of it, was that there was, again,
sentences.zh: 一个从默默无闻到成为首相的女性的故事，有一种神话般的弧光，这又一次让她与黛安娜联系在了一起。

sentences.en: a kind of mythic arc to the story of the woman who emerges from nowhere and becomes prime minister, which, again, aligns her with Diana.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，你知道的，我们确实有这两个神话般的人物，而且她们都是80年代的女性。

sentences.en: And it's interesting that the two, you know, we do have these two kind of mythic figures and they're both women in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 我想《王冠》大概就是以此为灵感展开的。

sentences.en: And I guess that that's what the crown will be riffing off.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的核心所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's what it's all about, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这一系列剧集都是在贩卖这个概念，对吧？

sentences.en: This series is all trading on that business, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说。

sentences.en: I mean.
sentences.zh: 但这确实表明，理解历史乃至以某种方式消费历史的一个关键方面，就是将其视作神话。

sentences.en: But it does suggest that a crucial aspect of how history is understood and, in a sense, consumed is as myth.
sentences.zh: 神话特质本身就具有历史意义。

sentences.en: The mythic qualities are themselves of historic significance.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，汤姆。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得你说的神话特质具有历史意义这一点，我也觉得很对，因为玛格丽特·撒切尔，我是说，她被观众消费的方式，就好像，

sentences.en: And I think where you say the mythic qualities are of historic significance, that seems to me right too, because Margaret Thatcher, I mean, she was consumed, as it were,
sentences.zh: 她要么是库伊拉，要么就是民众口中的——他们叫她什么来着？芬奇利的叶卡捷琳娜大帝？

sentences.en: by the audience as a sort of,
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: she's either Cruella de Vil, or she's the people, what do they call her, the Catherine the Great of Finchley?
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，她的崇拜者把她看作布狄卡、不列颠尼亚、伊丽莎白一世。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or she's, you know, her admirers see her as Boudicca, as Britannia, as Elizabeth I.
sentences.zh: 所以存在着这些，存在着这种对高贵女性、对被男人包围的爱国女性的持续神话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 还有女巫。

sentences.en: So there are these, there's this constant myth of the regal woman, of the patriotic woman surrounded by men.
sentences.zh: 对，还有女巫。

sentences.en: And the witch.
sentences.zh: 你觉得她扮演的是哪个角色，取决于你的政治立场。

sentences.en: Yeah, and the witch.
sentences.zh: 但人们总是把她放入这些神话般的角色中，对吧？

sentences.en: And which part you think she plays depends on your politics.
sentences.zh: 我是说，没有人会说她只是个普通的政治家，她只是个普通的职场女性。

sentences.en: But people always put her into these sort of mythic roles, don't they?
sentences.zh: 人们谈论她时，几乎把她当成超人一样，你知道的，

sentences.en: I mean, nobody just says she's a politician like any other, she's a working woman like any other.
sentences.zh: 达到了与谈论伊丽莎白一世、黛安娜或布狄卡相同的层级。

sentences.en: They talk about her almost as this superhuman, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者黛安娜，因为黛安娜同样也让人们产生了分歧。

sentences.en: on the same level that they talk about Elizabeth I or Diana or Boudicca.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她是人民心中的王妃，还是说她歇斯底里、没有骨气？

sentences.en: Well, or Diana, because Diana likewise was similarly divided people.
sentences.zh: 同样，全国对此也是意见不一。

sentences.en: You know, was she the queen of people's hearts or was she, you know, histrionic and lacking backbone.
sentences.zh: 不过我们对男性通常不会这样。

sentences.en: And again, the country was kind of divided on that.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: We don't really do that with men though.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许亨利八世算一个，但没几个。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有多少男性是让我们用这种二元对立的方式去谈论的。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe Henry VIII, but not many.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There aren't many men that we talk about in the same sort of dualistic way.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经无话可说了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们把整个80年代都聊完了吗？

sentences.en: We've run out of things to talk about, I think.
sentences.zh: 你知道还有很多没聊的吗？

sentences.en: Have we exhausted the whole of the 80s?
sentences.zh: 我们没聊托尼·本恩，没聊鲍比·桑兹，

sentences.en: Do you know what's on this so much?
sentences.zh: 肯·利文斯通，但这只是意味着过几个月我们得专门做一期关于1981年的播客。

sentences.en: We didn't talk about Tony Benn, we didn't talk about Bobby Sands,
sentences.zh: 哦，我告诉你你们漏掉了谁，是杜兰杜兰乐队（Duran Duran），

sentences.en: Ken Livingstone, but that just means we'll have to have another podcast all about 1981 in a few months' time.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·勒·邦（Simon Le Bon），以及我对你整本关于撒切尔时期著作的最爱的一句引言。

sentences.en: Oh, I'll tell you what you haven't mentioned is Duran Duran,
sentences.zh: 出自全部7000页的内容。

sentences.en: Simon Le Bon, and my favourite quote
sentences.zh: 其实，因为我为了这个做了功课，

sentences.en: in your entire book on the Thatcher period.
sentences.zh: 我这里有。

sentences.en: From all 7,000 pages.
sentences.zh: 这是关于《Union of the Snake》和《Hungry Like the Wolf》的。

sentences.en: Which actually, because I was swatting for this,
sentences.zh: 西蒙·勒·邦说，

sentences.en: I've got it here.
sentences.zh: 我一直喜欢T·S·艾略特（T.S. Eliot）这样稍微有点晦涩的诗人，这绝对是我歌词风格的一部分。

sentences.en: And this is with reference to Union of the Snake and Hungry Like the Wolf.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是这样。

sentences.en: Simon Le Bon said,
sentences.zh: 《荒原》本来可以是一首……

sentences.en: I've always liked poets like T.S.
sentences.zh: 《Planet Earth》和《荒原》。

sentences.en: Eliot who are a little bit obscure, and that's definitely part of my style, lyrically.
